why: W27 apply. `research/derived/pending/card_production_keys.json` was authored before W09 re-pointed eight vocab records and before W11a created five unlocks, so 2,946 authored rows do not cover the 2,951 production cards the course actually issues today. The Fable 100-row sample (research/reports/w27_sample_report.md) found exactly that gap and made it the apply's only authoring: 8 rows dropped and re-authored for the record their card now addresses, plus 5 rows for the cards that never had one. These 13 rows are that residue and nothing else in the W27 apply is authored.
definition: Same row shape as the campaign table: one row per (lesson, vocab slug) production card. `prompt` is a locale object because a bare `prompt_pt` is the contract violation design/i18n.md already names on speak_unit; `accept` is target-language Japanese and therefore locale-invariant. `accept` is NOT authored here either: it is the record's own forms[] minus the JMdict-tag strip the sample report ordered, computed by scripts/build_card_key_table.py exactly as it is for the other 2,938 rows, and repeated in `accept_expected` only so a reviewer can read the row without running the builder.
generated_by: W27 apply (hand-authored against corpus/vocab/*.json, the lesson body that issues the card, and research/derived/vocab_repoint_ledger.json for the list slot each re-point was made to).
sense_rule: `sense_index` names the sense the introducing lesson teaches, read out of the lesson's own prose where the lesson names it. For the eight re-pointed records the lesson prose predates the re-point in one case (les:n5-particulas-lugar-07 still describes 総, the retired lexeme), and there the sense is taken from the JLPT list row W09 re-pointed to, which is the evidence the re-point itself was made on.
prompt_overrides_why: One campaign row is rewritten here rather than in the campaign artifact, so the artifact stays the record of what W27 authored and the change stays visible. `audit_hygiene_all_locales.py` failed the apply on it: the prompt used `comboio`, which is pt-PT for a train and means a convoy in pt-BR (CLAUDE.md, Appendix B). One word, no change of sense, no change of accept set. Not authoring: a hygiene repair a hard gate forced.
